title: Super Senses! Animal Eyes, Ears and Noses for Kids
description:
Super senses! Pick your answer with Milo the bluebird, then find out how three animals see, hear and smell: a hippo has its eyes, ears and nose on top of its head so it can peek out of the water, a rhino cannot see very well but hears and smells super well, and a fox can hear tiny animals digging under the snow.
An interactive animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: Hippo eyes, ears and nostrils are on top of the head, so it can hear, see and breathe while most of its body is underwater (San Diego Zoo, zoo.sandiegozoo.org/animals/hippo); nostrils close before it goes under and the ears fold into a recess to close underwater (San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library fact sheet 'Hippopotamus', Physical Characteristics, read Nov 15 2026).

Mature hippos can stay under water for 5 minutes; hippos do not really swim, they move forward by punting off the river bottom; the herd leaves the water shortly before dark to graze (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Hippopotamus', Behavior & Ecology, read Nov 15 2026). Diet: grasses and other vegetation near rivers (same fact sheet, summary).

White rhino: poor eyesight, good sense of hearing, good sense of smell; the second largest land mammal, only surpassed in size by the elephant (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'White Rhinoceros', Physical Characteristics, read Nov 15 2026).

Rhino horn is made mainly of keratin, a protein also found in human hair and fingernails, and grows by around 2 cm each year (Save the Rhino International, 'What is rhino horn made of?', read Nov 15 2026).

Red foxes can hear the low-frequency sounds of small animals digging under the ground, leaves or snow; they stalk and pounce on prey; the tail is used for balance, warmth and signaling; adults have a dozen calls; young are called kits (Missouri Department of Conservation, 'What Red Foxes Say and Do', read Nov 15 2026).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about super senses!
How do animals see, hear and smell?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Get your eyes, ears and nose ready. Let's go!

segments.name: hippo

lines.t: Which animal can hide in the water, and still see, hear and breathe?
Is it the hippo? Or is it the horse?

lines: It is the hippo!
Here is the fun fact. A hippo's eyes, ears and nose are all on the top of its head.
So a hippo can stay in the water, with just its eyes and nose peeking out. Peekaboo!
Two eyes, two ears, and a nose with two holes. Let's count. One, two, three!

lines.t: What happens when the hippo goes all the way under the water? Hmm.

lines: Its nose closes tight, and its ears fold down. No water gets in!
close:hippo
A big hippo can stay under the water for about five minutes!
And here is a surprise. Hippos do not really swim. They push off the bottom of the river, and bounce along!
When the sun goes down, the hippo comes out to munch on grass. Munch, munch, munch!
Say it with me. Eyes, ears and nose on top!
close:host
Can you peek like a hippo? Hide down low, then peek your eyes out. Peekaboo!
Now close your nose, like a hippo going under. Hold it! And let go!

lines.t: Quick check! Can a hippo close its nose under the water? Yes, or no?

lines: Yes! Its nose closes tight. Great job!

short.title: Why Are a Hippo's Eyes on Top of Its Head?

segments.name: rhino

lines.t: Who has a big horn on its nose?
Is it the cow? Or is it the rhino?

lines: It is the rhino!
Here is the fun fact. A rhino cannot see very well.
But a rhino has super ears, and a super nose! It can hear and smell very, very well.

lines.t: Now look at the rhino's horn. What do you think it is made of?

lines: The same stuff as your fingernails! Look at your fingernails. Tap, tap, tap!
A rhino's horn keeps growing a little bit every year, just like your nails.
close:rhino
A rhino's skin is thick, with deep folds. Like a big, gray coat!
And a rhino is very, very big. The white rhino is the second biggest animal on land.
Who is the biggest? The elephant! Only the elephant is bigger than the white rhino.
A rhino has a wide, flat lip, for munching on grass. Munch, munch!
Say it with me. A rhino has a super nose!
close:host
Can you sniff like a rhino? Sniff, sniff, sniff!
Now put your hands by your ears, and listen like a rhino. Listen!

lines.t: Quick check! A rhino's horn is made of the same stuff as what? Your nails? Or wood?

lines: Your nails! Tap, tap, tap. Super thinking!

short.title: What Is a Rhino's Horn Made Of? Rhino Facts

segments.name: fox

lines.t: Who can hear a tiny mouse digging under the snow?
Is it the fox? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the fox!
Here is the fun fact. A fox has super ears! It can hear tiny animals digging under the ground, under the leaves, or under the snow.
Look at those big, pointy ears. They listen, listen, listen.

lines.t: The fox hears a tiny sound under the snow. What does it do next? Hmm.

lines: It sneaks up, jumps high, and pounces! Boing!
Now look at the fox's big, bushy tail.
close:fox
The tail helps the fox balance, and it keeps the fox warm.
A grown-up fox can make about twelve different calls. Wow, that is a lot!
Baby foxes are called kits.
Kits grow up in a cozy den, and the den has a back door too!
Say it with me. A fox has super ears!
close:host
Can you pounce like a fox? Crouch down low. And jump! Boing!
Now listen, listen, like a fox. What can you hear?

lines.t: Quick check! What helps the fox keep warm? Its tail? Or its ears?

lines: Its tail! A big, bushy tail. You remembered!

short.title: A Fox Can Hear a Mouse Under the Snow!

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We met three friends with super senses. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who has its eyes, ears and nose on the top of its head?
Whose horn is made of the same stuff as your nails?
Who can hear a tiny mouse under the snow?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Peek like a hippo. Sniff like a rhino. And pounce like a fox!
Which super sense is your favorite?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
